question:
The system
$$x+2y-z=3$$
$$2x+4y-2z=7$$
$$x-y+z=1$$
is proposed to have a solution.

(a) Evaluate the determinant of its coefficient matrix.

(b) Compare the first two equations and examine whether they can hold simultaneously.

(c) Hence, determine the consistency and number of solutions of the system.
explanation:
(a)
The coefficient matrix is
$$A=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & -1\\2 & 4 & -2\\1 & -1 & 1\end{bmatrix}$$
Since the second row is twice the first row,
$$R_2=2R_1$$
Therefore,
$$|A|=0$$

(b)
Multiplying the first equation by $2$ gives
$$2x+4y-2z=6$$
However, the second equation states
$$2x+4y-2z=7$$
The same expression cannot be equal to both $6$ and $7$. Therefore, the first two equations cannot hold simultaneously.

(c)
The system contains a contradiction and is therefore inconsistent. Hence, it has no solution.

options.A:
(a) $|A|=0$
(b) The second equation is exactly twice the first equation
(c) The system has infinitely many solutions
options.B:
(a) $|A|=0$
(b) Twice the first equation gives $2x+4y-2z=6$, which contradicts $2x+4y-2z=7$
(c) The system is inconsistent and has no solution
options.C:
(a) $|A|=1$
(b) The first two equations are independent
(c) The system has a unique solution
options.D:
(a) $|A|=0$
(b) The first two equations can hold only when $x=y=z=0$
(c) The system has exactly one solution
